L25: 
L26: July 24, 2026
L27: 
L28: For Diwali, reach for a linen cotton blend in a warm, rich shade: a wine red shirt or a deep indigo kurta for the evening, and a lighter ivory or gold tone for the morning puja. The blend breathes through long celebrations, holds a clean line in photographs, and creases far less than pure linen, which is exactly what a full festive day asks for.
L29: House of Suave dresses the whole festive week from one honest fabric. Every kurta and shirt below is a linen cotton blend, so you get the cool, natural feel of linen with the durability and lower creasing of cotton. Here is how to build a Diwali wardrobe that carries you from the morning puja to a late evening of lights, sweets, and photographs.
L30: ## Why a linen cotton blend suits Diwali
L31: Diwali days are long. You move between kitchens warm with cooking, crowded living rooms, terraces, and cars. A pure linen shirt would crumple by the second round of guests. A heavy synthetic would trap heat around the diyas and candles. The linen cotton blend sits between the two: it stays cool and light, it recovers its shape as you move, and it photographs crisp under warm festive lighting. That is why it works as well for a morning puja as it does for a night of fireworks.
L32: Burgundy Royale Linen Shirt, a deep wine red with a mandarin collar. Rs 1,999, sizes L to 10XL.
L33: ## The evening look: deep, warm, and celebratory
L34: 
L35: Evening is when Diwali dressing earns its keep. Warm, saturated shades read beautifully against strings of lights and against the reds and golds most homes lean into.
L36: ### Burgundy Royale, the new wine red shirt
L37: Our newest launch, the cite7†Burgundy Royale Linen Shirt , was made for evenings like these. It is a rich wine red, deeper than a classic red and more distinctive than maroon, with warm undertones and a clean mandarin collar that needs no tie and no fuss. Worn over dark trousers with leather sandals or loafers, it looks considered without looking like you tried too hard. It is a premium linen cotton blend, bio washed for softness, priced at Rs 1,999 and made to order in sizes L to 10XL.
L38: ### Midnight Indigo for a quieter statement
L39: 
L40: If red is not your colour, a deep blue does the same evening job with more restraint. The cite8†Midnight Indigo Linen Blend Kurta Shirt is a dark, inky tone that pairs with almost any bottom and sets off gold or brass jewellery cleanly. At Rs 1,949 in sizes L to 10XL, it is an easy hero for a dinner or a card night.
L41: 
L42: Midnight Indigo Linen Blend Kurta Shirt. Rs 1,949, sizes L to 10XL.
L43: ## The morning puja: light and easy
L44: The morning puja calls for something calm and comfortable that still looks intentional. Soft, light shades suit the daylight and stay cool while you sit through the ritual. The cite9†Tuscan Ivory Linen Blend Kurta Shirt is our pick here: a warm off white that works with a simple pyjama or with churidar, and takes a light shawl or Nehru jacket well if the morning is cool. It is Rs 1,949 in sizes L to 10XL.
L45: Ivory also has a practical advantage on a busy day, since it hides very little and reads fresh in every photograph.
L46: ## Warm reds for family gatherings
L47: For the family lunch or the afternoon of visits, a warm red kurta strikes the right festive note without going formal. The cite10†Siena Rouge Linen Blend Kurta Shirt is a deep terracotta red that feels celebratory and grounded at once, and it flatters a wide range of skin tones. Pair it with ivory or beige bottoms to keep it light, or with black to push it towards evening. It is Rs 1,949 in sizes L to 10XL.
L48: If you want a brighter pop, the cite11†Tangerine Muse Linen Blend Kurta Shirt brings a citrus warmth that photographs vividly against festive decor.
L49: ## Relaxed evenings and card nights
L50: 
L51: Not every Diwali evening is formal. For card nights and casual get togethers, a Cuban collar shirt is the relaxed choice. The cite12†Ravenna Noir Striped Cuban Linen Shirt has an open, camp style collar and a subtle stripe that dresses down without looking careless. Wear it loose over trousers with the top button open. It is a made to order linen cotton blend at Rs 1,949 in sizes L to 10XL. You can see the full set on the cite13†Cuban linen shirts collection .
L52: ## Colour and pairing notes
L53: A few simple rules make festive dressing easier. Warm shades like wine red, terracotta, and tangerine sit well against the reds and golds of Diwali decor, so keep bottoms neutral to let the colour lead. Deep tones like indigo and black photograph cleanly at night and make gold or brass accessories stand out. Light tones like ivory belong to the morning and to warm daylight. Across all of them, footwear in tan or dark brown leather keeps the look warm and finished.
L54: For more on taking one shirt from day to night, read our guide on how to cite14†style a linen shirt from office to evening .
L55: ## Sizing and fit for the festive week
L56: 
L57: Festive days mean sitting on floors, second helpings, and long hours in one outfit, so comfort matters. Every style here comes in sizes L to 10XL, cut for a range of builds rather than a single standard fit. If you are between sizes, size up for a relaxed drape that moves with you through the day. Browse the full range on the cite15†kurta shirts collection .
L58: 
L59: ## Frequently asked questions
L60: ### What should a man wear for Diwali?
L61: 
L62: For the morning puja, choose a light shade such as ivory in a breathable linen cotton blend. For the evening, choose a warm, deep shade such as wine red or indigo. A linen cotton blend keeps you cool through a long day and creases far less than pure linen.
L63: ### Are linen blend shirts good for festive occasions?
L64: 
L65: Yes. A linen cotton blend has the cool, natural look of linen with the durability and lower creasing of cotton, so it holds a clean line through hours of celebration and photographs crisply under warm festive lighting.
L66: ### Which colours suit Diwali?
L67: 
L68: Warm and deep shades suit Diwali well. Wine red, terracotta, and tangerine echo the festive palette, while indigo and black read elegantly at night and set off gold jewellery. Keep bottoms neutral so the colour leads.
L69: ### Do these shirts come in larger sizes?
L70: 
L71: Yes. Every kurta and shirt here is available in sizes L to 10XL, cut to suit bigger builds as well as standard fits.

L92: Sansevieria Festive Style Guide
L93: 
L94: You want to look festive—but still feel like yourself. You want something special enough for the celebration, comfortable enough to enjoy it, and versatile enough to wear again when the diyas are put away.
L95: 
L96: That is where a modern festive wardrobe can become simpler.
L97: Instead of choosing between everyday western wear and heavily embellished occasion clothing, an embroidered cotton or linen shirt can sit beautifully in between.
L98: 
L99: Styled with flowing trousers, skirts, jewellery and festive footwear, an embroidered shirt can move from an office Diwali party to a family lunch, puja, dinner or intimate celebration—without making you feel overdressed.
L100: Quick answer: What can women wear for a modern Indian festive look? A modern festive outfit can combine an embroidered cotton or linen shirt with palazzo trousers, a long skirt or tonal wide-leg pants. Add jewellery, festive footwear and one thoughtful accessory to make the outfit feel celebration-ready without making it heavy.
L101: ## Festive Dressing Should Feel Special—Not Uncomfortable
L102: 
L103: The question “What should I wear?” often hides several smaller questions.
L104: 
L105:   * Will I look festive enough?
L106:   * Will everyone else be more dressed up?
L107:   * Is this too casual for a family gathering?
L108:   * Can I comfortably wear it for several hours?
L109:   * Will I ever wear it again after the festival?
L110:   * Most importantly, does it actually feel like me?
L111: 
L112: A good festive outfit does not need to answer these questions with more embellishment.
L113: Sometimes the better answer is better fabric, thoughtful embroidery, a beautiful colour and intentional styling.
L114: ## 1. “I Want to Look Festive, but I Don't Like Heavy Festive Clothes”
L115: 
L116: Not every Diwali dinner, family puja or festive lunch needs layers of embellishment.
L117: 
L118: If your personal style is understated, begin with a cite3†women's embroidered cotton shirt and let the embroidery become the decorative element.
L119: 
L120: Warm ivory embroidered shirt + cream palazzo trousers + gold earrings + festive flats
